KJV.text: For innumerable evils have compassed me about: mine iniquities have taken hold upon me, so that I am not able to look up; they are more than the hairs of mine head: therefore my heart faileth me.
KJV.displayText: For innumerable evils have compassed me about: mine iniquities have taken hold upon me, so that I am not able to look up; they are more than the hairs of mine head: therefore my heart faileth me.

BSB.text: For evils without number surround me; my sins have overtaken me, so that I cannot see. They are more than the hairs of my head, and my heart has failed within me.
BSB.displayText: For evils without number surround me; my sins have overtaken me, so that I cannot see. They are more than the hairs of my head, and my heart has failed within me.

verses.context: Shortly after thanking God for a past rescue, David finds himself surrounded by troubles again and overwhelmed by the weight of his own sins.

KJV.text: My soul thirsteth for God, for the living God: when shall I come and appear before God?
KJV.displayText: My soul thirsteth for God, for the living God: when shall I come and appear before God?

BSB.displayText: My soul thirsts for God, the living God. When shall I come and appear in God’s presence?

CPDV.displayText: My soul has thirsted for the strong living God. When will I draw close and appear before the face of God?

verses.context: In this psalm of the sons of Korah, a writer far from the temple longs for the day he can come and stand in God's presence again.

KJV.text: Deep calleth unto deep at the noise of thy waterspouts: all thy waves and thy billows are gone over me.
KJV.displayText: Deep calleth unto deep at the noise of thy waterspouts: all thy waves and thy billows are gone over me.

BSB.text: Deep calls to deep in the roar of Your waterfalls; all Your breakers and waves have rolled over me.
BSB.displayText: Deep calls to deep in the roar of Your waterfalls; all Your breakers and waves have rolled over me.

CPDV.text: Abyss calls upon abyss, with the voice of your floodgate. All your heights and your waves have passed over me.
CPDV.displayText: Abyss calls upon abyss, with the voice of your floodgate. All your heights and your waves have passed over me.

verses.context: Remembering God from far away, near the Jordan and Mount Hermon, the writer of this psalm feels sorrow crashing over him like deep waters.

KJV.text: Yea, for thy sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.
KJV.displayText: Yea, for thy sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.

BSB.text: Yet for Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered.
BSB.displayText: Yet for Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered.

CPDV.text: will not God find this out? For he knows the secrets of the heart. For, because of you, we are being killed all day long. We are considered as sheep for the slaughter.
CPDV.displayText: will not God find this out? For he knows the secrets of the heart. For, because of you, we are being killed all day long. We are considered as sheep for the slaughter.

verses.context: In a lament by the sons of Korah, the nation protests it has stayed loyal to God yet suffers anyway, a line Paul later quotes in Romans.

KJV.text: Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.
KJV.displayText: Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.

BSB.text: Against You, You only, have I sinned and done what is evil in Your sight, so that You may be proved right when You speak and blameless when You judge.
BSB.displayText: Against You, You only, have I sinned and done what is evil in Your sight, so that You may be proved right when You speak and blameless when You judge.

CPDV.text: Against you only have I sinned, and I have done evil before your eyes. And so, you are justified in your words, and you will prevail when you give judgment.
CPDV.displayText: Against you only have I sinned, and I have done evil before your eyes. And so, you are justified in your words, and you will prevail when you give judgment.

verses.context: Pleading for mercy after Nathan exposed his adultery with Bathsheba and the death of Uriah, David faces God with the full truth of what he has done.

KJV.text: Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom.
KJV.displayText: Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom.

BSB.text: Surely You desire truth in the inmost being; You teach me wisdom in the inmost place.
BSB.displayText: Surely You desire truth in the inmost being; You teach me wisdom in the inmost place.

CPDV.text: For behold, you have loved truth. The obscure and hidden things of your wisdom, you have manifested to me.
CPDV.displayText: For behold, you have loved truth. The obscure and hidden things of your wisdom, you have manifested to me.

verses.context: In his prayer of repentance after his sin with Bathsheba, David says God wants honesty deep inside a person, and asks God to teach him wisdom there.

KJV.text: Make me to hear joy and gladness; that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.
KJV.displayText: Make me to hear joy and gladness; that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.

BSB.text: Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones You have crushed rejoice.
BSB.displayText: Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones You have crushed rejoice.

CPDV.text: In my hearing, you will grant gladness and rejoicing. And the bones that have been humbled will exult.
CPDV.displayText: In my hearing, you will grant gladness and rejoicing. And the bones that have been humbled will exult.

verses.context: Crushed by guilt after Nathan exposed his sin with Bathsheba, David asks God to let him hear joy again and make his broken bones rejoice.

KJV.text: For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it: neither was it he that hated me that did magnify himself against me; then I would have hid myself from him:

BSB.text: For it is not an enemy who insults me; that I could endure. It is not a foe who rises against me; from him I could hide.
BSB.displayText: For it is not an enemy who insults me; that I could endure. It is not a foe who rises against me; from him I could hide.

CPDV.displayText: For if my enemy had spoken evil about me, certainly, I would have sustained it. And if he who hated me had been speaking great things against me, I would perhaps have hidden myself from him.

verses.context: Surrounded by violence in the city, David says what hurts most is that the one attacking him is not an enemy but a close friend.

KJV.text: Trust not in oppression, and become not vain in robbery: if riches increase, set not your heart upon them.
KJV.displayText: Trust not in oppression, and become not vain in robbery: if riches increase, set not your heart upon them.

BSB.text: Place no trust in extortion, or false hope in stolen goods. If your riches increase, do not set your heart upon them.
BSB.displayText: Place no trust in extortion, or false hope in stolen goods. If your riches increase, do not set your heart upon them.

CPDV.text: Do not trust in iniquity, and do not desire plunder. If riches flow toward you, do not be willing to set your heart on them.
CPDV.displayText: Do not trust in iniquity, and do not desire plunder. If riches flow toward you, do not be willing to set your heart on them.

verses.context: Having called God his only rock and refuge, David warns his listeners not to trust in extortion or set their hearts on growing wealth.

KJV.text: Thou hast caused men to ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water: but thou broughtest us out into a wealthy place.
KJV.displayText: Thou hast caused men to ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water: but thou broughtest us out into a wealthy place.

BSB.displayText: You let men ride over our heads; we went through fire and water, but You brought us into abundance.

CPDV.text: You have set men over our heads. We have crossed through fire and water. And you have led us out to refreshment.
CPDV.displayText: You have set men over our heads. We have crossed through fire and water. And you have led us out to refreshment.

verses.context: In this thanksgiving psalm with no named author, the writer looks back on the hard trials God's people went through and where God brought them.

KJV.text: If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me:
KJV.displayText: If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me:

BSB.text: If I had cherished iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
BSB.displayText: If I had cherished iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.

CPDV.displayText: If I have seen iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not heed me.

verses.context: Telling others what God has done for him, the writer of this thanksgiving psalm admits that God would not have listened if he had held on to sin.

KJV.text: God setteth the solitary in families: he bringeth out those which are bound with chains: but the rebellious dwell in a dry land.
KJV.displayText: God setteth the solitary in families: he bringeth out those which are bound with chains: but the rebellious dwell in a dry land.

BSB.text: God settles the lonely in families; He leads the prisoners out to prosperity, but the rebellious dwell in a sun-scorched land.
BSB.displayText: God settles the lonely in families; He leads the prisoners out to prosperity, but the rebellious dwell in a sun-scorched land.

CPDV.text: It is God who makes men dwell in a house under one custom. He leads out those who are strongly bound, and similarly, those who exasperate, who dwell in sepulchers.
CPDV.displayText: It is God who makes men dwell in a house under one custom. He leads out those who are strongly bound, and similarly, those who exasperate, who dwell in sepulchers.

verses.context: In a psalm celebrating God as a father to the fatherless, David adds that God gives lonely people a family and leads prisoners into freedom.

KJV.text: I sink in deep mire, where there is no standing: I am come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me.
KJV.displayText: I sink in deep mire, where there is no standing: I am come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me.

BSB.displayText: I have sunk into the miry depths, where there is no footing; I have drifted into deep waters, where the flood engulfs me.

CPDV.text: I have become stuck in a deep quagmire, and there is no firm footing. I have arrived at the height of the sea, and a tempest has overwhelmed me.
CPDV.displayText: I have become stuck in a deep quagmire, and there is no firm footing. I have arrived at the height of the sea, and a tempest has overwhelmed me.

verses.context: Hated without cause by many enemies, David describes himself sinking in deep mud with no footing, as floodwaters close over him.

KJV.text: Now also when I am old and grayheaded, O God, forsake me not; until I have shewed thy strength unto this generation, and thy power to every one that is to come.
KJV.displayText: Now also when I am old and grayheaded, O God, forsake me not; until I have shewed thy strength unto this generation, and thy power to every one that is to come.

BSB.displayText: Even when I am old and gray, do not forsake me, O God, until I proclaim Your power to the next generation, Your might to all who are to come.

CPDV.text: even in old age and with grey hairs. Do not abandon me, O God, while I announce your arm to every future generation: your power
CPDV.displayText: even in old age and with grey hairs. Do not abandon me, O God, while I announce your arm to every future generation: your power

verses.context: Now old and gray, the writer of this psalm asks God not to abandon him until he has told the next generation what God has done.

KJV.text: Thou shalt increase my greatness, and comfort me on every side.
KJV.displayText: Thou shalt increase my greatness, and comfort me on every side.

BSB.text: You will increase my honor and comfort me once again.
BSB.displayText: You will increase my honor and comfort me once again.

CPDV.text: You have multiplied your magnificence. And so, turning back to me, you have consoled me.
CPDV.displayText: You have multiplied your magnificence. And so, turning back to me, you have consoled me.

verses.context: Looking back on many troubles in a long life, the aging writer of this psalm trusts God to restore his honor and comfort him again.

KJV.text: For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all.
KJV.displayText: For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all.

BSB.text: For God has consigned everyone to disobedience so that He may have mercy on everyone.
BSB.displayText: For God has consigned everyone to disobedience so that He may have mercy on everyone.

CPDV.text: For God has enclosed everyone in unbelief, so that he may have mercy on everyone.
CPDV.displayText: For God has enclosed everyone in unbelief, so that he may have mercy on everyone.

verses.context: Ending his long reflection on Israel and the Gentiles, Paul concludes that God's purpose behind everyone's disobedience is mercy for all.

KJV.text: I remembered God, and was troubled: I complained, and my spirit was overwhelmed. Selah.
KJV.displayText: I remembered God, and was troubled: I complained, and my spirit was overwhelmed.

BSB.displayText: I remembered You, O God, and I groaned; I mused and my spirit grew faint.

CPDV.displayText: I was mindful of God, and I was delighted, and I was distressed, and my spirit fell away.

verses.context: In a sleepless time of trouble, Asaph admits that even thinking about God, which should have comforted him, only made him groan.

KJV.text: O Lord God of hosts, how long wilt thou be angry against the prayer of thy people?
KJV.displayText: O Lord God of hosts, how long wilt thou be angry against the prayer of thy people?

BSB.text: O LORD God of Hosts, how long will Your anger smolder against the prayers of Your people?
BSB.displayText: O LORD God of Hosts, how long will Your anger smolder against the prayers of Your people?

CPDV.text: O Lord, God of hosts, how long will you be angry over the prayer of your servant?
CPDV.displayText: O Lord, God of hosts, how long will you be angry over the prayer of your servant?

verses.context: In a prayer for a nation in ruins, Asaph asks the God of Israel how long he will stay angry even while his people keep praying.

KJV.text: Turn us, O God of our salvation, and cause thine anger toward us to cease.
KJV.displayText: Turn us, O God of our salvation, and cause thine anger toward us to cease.

BSB.text: Restore us, O God of our salvation, and put away Your displeasure toward us.
BSB.displayText: Restore us, O God of our salvation, and put away Your displeasure toward us.

CPDV.text: Convert us, O God, our Savior, and turn your anger away from us.
CPDV.displayText: Convert us, O God, our Savior, and turn your anger away from us.

verses.context: After recalling how God once forgave his people and restored the land, the sons of Korah ask God to restore them again and set aside his anger.

KJV.text: Be merciful unto me, O Lord: for I cry unto thee daily.
KJV.displayText: Be merciful unto me, O Lord: for I cry unto thee daily.

BSB.displayText: Be merciful to me, O Lord, for I call to You all day long.

CPDV.displayText: O Lord, be merciful to me, for I have cried out to you all day long.

verses.context: In a prayer where he calls himself poor and needy, David asks God to be merciful to him, since he calls out to God all day long.

KJV.text: Mine eye mourneth by reason of affliction: Lord, I have called daily upon thee, I have stretched out my hands unto thee.
KJV.displayText: Mine eye mourneth by reason of affliction: Lord, I have called daily upon thee, I have stretched out my hands unto thee.

BSB.displayText: My eyes grow dim with grief. I call to You daily, O LORD; I spread out my hands to You.

CPDV.displayText: My eyes languished before destitution. All day long, I cried out to you, O Lord. I stretched out my hands to you.

verses.context: In this bleak psalm of the sons of Korah, credited to Heman the Ezrahite, the writer tells God his eyes are dim with grief as he calls out every day.

KJV.text: Shall thy wonders be known in the dark? and thy righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?
KJV.displayText: Shall thy wonders be known in the dark? and thy righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?

BSB.text: Will Your wonders be known in the darkness, or Your righteousness in the land of oblivion?
BSB.displayText: Will Your wonders be known in the darkness, or Your righteousness in the land of oblivion?

CPDV.displayText: Will your wonders be known in the darkness, or your justice in the land of oblivion?

verses.context: Feeling close to death in one of the darkest psalms, Heman asks God whether his wonders and goodness can be known in the grave.

KJV.text: The days of our years are threescore years and ten; and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years, yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.

BSB.displayText: The length of our days is seventy years— or eighty if we are strong— yet their pride is but labor and sorrow, for they quickly pass, and we fly away.

CPDV.displayText: The days of our years in them are seventy years. But in the powerful, they are eighty years, and more of these are with hardship and sorrow. For mildness has overwhelmed us, and we shall be corrected.

verses.context: Moses, in the psalm credited to him, weighs the short span of a human life, seventy or eighty years, against God's everlasting existence.

KJV.text: Return, O Lord, how long? and let it repent thee concerning thy servants.
KJV.displayText: Return, O Lord, how long? and let it repent thee concerning thy servants.

BSB.displayText: Return, O LORD! How long will it be? Have compassion on Your servants.

CPDV.displayText: Return, O Lord, how long? And may you be persuaded on behalf of your servants.

verses.context: After asking God to teach his people to number their days, Moses pleads with God to return and have compassion on his servants.

KJV.text: Make us glad according to the days wherein thou hast afflicted us, and the years wherein we have seen evil.

BSB.displayText: Make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen evil.

CPDV.displayText: We have been rejoicing, because of the days in which you humbled us, because of the years in which we saw evils.

verses.context: Near the end of his prayer about life's brevity, Moses asks God to give his people as many years of gladness as they have had of trouble.

CPDV.displayText: A thousand will fall before your side and ten thousand before your right hand. Yet it will not draw near you.

verses.context: In this psalm about the safety of those who shelter in God, the psalm's writer promises that disaster may strike thousands nearby yet not reach them.

KJV.text: He that planted the ear, shall he not hear? he that formed the eye, shall he not see?
KJV.displayText: He that planted the ear, shall he not hear? he that formed the eye, shall he not see?

CPDV.displayText: He who formed the ear, will he not hear? And he who forged the eye, does he not look closely?

verses.context: Answering people who crush the weak while claiming that God does not see, the psalm's writer asks whether the one who made the eye cannot see.

CPDV.displayText: Come, let us exult in the Lord. Let us shout joyfully to God, our Savior.

verses.context: With no named author, this psalm opens by calling God's people to gather and sing loudly to God, the rock who saves them.

BSB.displayText: My heart is afflicted, and withered like grass; I even forget to eat my bread.
